references.text: Joseph made the children of Israel swear that they would carry his bones out of Egypt when God visited them. This is the original oath that Moses fulfills in Exodus 13:19.
Joseph's bones, which the Israelites had brought with them from Egypt, were buried in Shechem. This is the final fulfillment of what Moses began in Exodus 13:19.
Stephen mentions in his speech that Jacob and the fathers were brought to Shechem, which includes Joseph's bones that were taken out of Egypt.
The book of Hebrews notes that Joseph, in faith, spoke about the Israelites' departure from Egypt and gave instructions concerning his bones. This refers directly to the oath that Moses fulfills.
Jacob made Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan. This shows the tradition of swearing an oath regarding burial in the promised land, which Joseph later continues.
This is the direct source of the oath that Moses later fulfills by taking Joseph's bones with him.
Jacob's prophecy about God leading them home (Gen 48) is the theological foundation for Joseph's oath to take his bones along (Exod 13).
